context: I Theorem 1.3 (Hardness of AND Subset Sum). Assuming ∀∃-SETH, there are no ε, δ > 0 such that the following problem can be solved in time O(N 1+δ−ε ): Given N Subset Sum instances, each with O(N ε ) integers and target O(N δ ), determine whether all of these instances are yes-instances. Note that in comparison with the OR Subset Sum case (Theorem 1.2), the size of our instances is polynomial O(N ε ) instead of logarithmic Oδ,ε (log N ). We leave it as an open problem whether this is inherent or Theorem 1.3 can be improved. It follows from Theorem 1.3 that AND Subset Sum on N instances, each on at most s integers and with target at most t, cannot be solved in time O(N e s + t(N s)1−ε ). We show that the same holds for the Partition problem, which is the special case of Subset Sum where the target is half of the total input sum. This is the starting point for our reductions in the next section. I Corollary 1.4.
